_comment: Original writing for art.mystery, art.rivals and art.legend. {port} = the next port to visit, {rival} = rival company name.

mystery.title: The Marigold's Missing Cargo
mystery.intro: The coaster Marigold vanished with forty sealed crates. Her owner is dead, her crew scattered, and the insurers would like a word.
chapters: A dock clerk remembers the Marigold's mate drinking in {port}. Sail there and ask around.
The mate is long gone, but he paid his tab with a pawn ticket from {port}.
The pawnbroker sold the item to a lighthouse keeper. The keeper's lamp burns at {port}.
The keeper used the crate lid as a shelf. Its stencil reads a warehouse number at {port}.
The warehouse ledger shows the crates were shipped on to {port}, under a false name.
mystery.end: In the last warehouse, behind sacks of grain, the forty crates sit untouched. Inside: the Marigold's logbooks, every one. She was never lost; she was hidden, to keep a secret trade route safe. The route is long gone. The story is yours.

rivals.spotted: {rival} has been watching your ledger. They are just ahead of you, and they know it.
rivals.chasing: {rival} is still ahead. Their captains toast your name, but not kindly.
rivals.overtook: You have passed {rival}. Word is their owner threw a teapot across the counting house.
rivals.holding: {rival} is behind you and closing. Keep the holds full.
rivals.lost: {rival} slipped past you in the night. The harbour gossips are thrilled.
rivals.top: There is no one above you. {rival} is the closest challenger. Every captain on the sea wants your berth.

legend.intro: Old crews talk of the Lantern Queen, a freighter with every lamp lit and nobody at the wheel. To find her you need three pieces of the chart she was last seen on.
legend.chart: A piece of the chart is said to lie at {port}.
legend.ready: Your chart is whole. Wait for a sighting, then be docked at the port she haunts while she is there.
legend.found: You saw her. Close enough to read the brass on her stern: 'Carried what was asked. Asked nothing back.' The crews will be telling this one for years.
